name: Moving warm-up
purpose: Raise your heart rate and loosen hips, shoulders and wrists before you hit a ball.

variants.instructions: One minute each: easy jog on the spot, side steps left and right, arm circles forward and back, hip circles, wrist rolls, then 10 slow lunges with a twist toward your forehand side.

success.description: You feel warm and slightly out of breath.

coachingPoints: Start slow and build up
Big, easy movements, no bouncing stretches
Finish in your ready position

name: Skip and shuffle warm-up
purpose: A livelier warm-up with small jumps to wake up the legs.

variants.instructions: Rope or imaginary rope: 3 rounds of 40 seconds skipping and 20 seconds rest. Then 2 rounds of fast side shuffles across 3 metres, touching the floor at each end. End with arm and wrist circles.

coachingPoints: Stay on the balls of your feet
Land softly
Keep your knees bent on the shuffles

name: Ball on the bat
purpose: Build soft hands and ball feel: the ball should feel light on the bat.

variants.instructions: Bounce the ball up on the bat about 20 cm high. Then switch faces every bounce (red, black, red…). Then walk while you bounce. Count your best run of alternating bounces.
Stand one metre from the wall and tap the ball gently against it with your forehand, letting it bounce once on the floor if needed. Then switch to backhand.

success.description: 30 alternating bounces without dropping the ball.

coachingPoints: Loose grip, soft wrist
Watch the ball onto the bat
Small, quiet touches

name: Forehand warm-up rally
purpose: Find your rhythm and timing with easy forehand rallies.

variants.instructions: Forehand to forehand, corner to corner, at a medium pace. Start slow and speed up a little each minute.
Feeder sends easy topspin to your forehand corner, one ball every second and a half. Hit cross-court.
variants.feederInstructions: Feed light topspin to their forehand corner at a steady rhythm. Same height and speed every ball.

variants.instructions: Set the robot to light topspin, medium speed, one spot on your forehand. Hit cross-court.
With the rebound board up, hit easy forehands at it and back onto your half. Keep a steady rhythm.

success.description: 20 forehands in a row at an easy pace.

coachingPoints: Relax first, speed later
Turn your waist, don't just swing the arm
Recover to ready after each hit

name: Backhand warm-up rally
purpose: Settle the backhand with easy rallies before the real work.

variants.instructions: Backhand to backhand, corner to corner, at a medium pace.
Feeder sends easy topspin to your backhand. Hit back diagonally.
variants.feederInstructions: Feed light topspin to their backhand corner, same rhythm each ball.

variants.instructions: Robot on light topspin to your backhand corner. Hit cross-court.
Rebound board up. Easy backhands against it, keeping the ball in front of your body.

success.description: 20 backhands in a row at an easy pace.

coachingPoints: Bat in front of your belly button
Elbow relaxed, slightly forward
Short stroke, quick reset

name: Forehand drive, cross-court
purpose: Groove a repeatable forehand drive: same swing, same contact, every ball.

variants.instructions: Forehand cross-court rally. Count your longest run without a miss. When you reach the target, aim deeper: last 30 cm of the table.
One ball at a time to your forehand. Hit each one cross-court, deep. Sets of 20 balls, short rest between sets.
variants.feederInstructions: Light topspin to their forehand, one ball every 1.5 seconds. Keep it steady and the same height.

variants.instructions: Robot to your forehand, light topspin, one spot, about 40 balls a minute. Hit cross-court and count your run.
Rebound board up. Forehand drives with a steady rhythm. Count your run without a miss.

coachingPoints: Turn the waist back and through
Contact at the top of the bounce, in front
Finish with the bat near your forehead, then recover

name: Backhand drive, cross-court
purpose: A steady backhand drive you can trust in a rally.

variants.instructions: Backhand cross-court rally. Count your longest run. Then aim deeper.
Sets of 20 balls to your backhand. Hit each one diagonally and deep.
variants.feederInstructions: Light topspin to their backhand, steady rhythm.

variants.instructions: Robot to your backhand, light topspin, one spot. Hit cross-court and count your run.
Rebound board up. Backhand drives, ball in front of your body. Count your run.

coachingPoints: Bat starts in front of your stomach
Forearm moves forward and slightly up
Stop the bat pointing at your target

name: Backhand push rally
purpose: Keep a backspin ball low and safe with a short, controlled push.

variants.instructions: Backhand push to backhand push, diagonally. Keep every ball low over the net. Count your run.
Feeder sends backspin to your backhand. Push each ball back diagonally and low.
variants.feederInstructions: Feed backspin with a chopping action to their backhand, medium length.

variants.instructions: Robot on backspin to your backhand, slow speed. Push back diagonally.

success.description: 20 pushes in a row, all low over the net.

coachingPoints: Open the bat face
Move forward and slightly down under the ball
Short follow-through, then back to ready

name: Forehand push rally
purpose: A calm forehand push you can use against short backspin.

variants.instructions: Forehand push to forehand push, diagonally. Step in with your right foot (left if left-handed) for short balls.
Backspin balls to your forehand. Push back diagonally and low.
variants.feederInstructions: Backspin to their forehand, medium length.

variants.instructions: Robot on backspin to your forehand. Push back diagonally.

coachingPoints: Step in toward the ball
Bat face open, contact under the back of the ball
Return to ready, don't stay leaning in

name: Easy feed, first contact
purpose: First hits with a new stroke: slow, regular balls to one spot so you can focus on the shape.

variants.instructions: Play the stroke you are learning. Feeder sends one slow ball at a time to one spot. Sets of 10, a short pause, then check your shape against the three cues.
variants.feederInstructions: Slow, easy balls to one spot. Wait until they are back in ready before the next ball.

variants.instructions: Robot at its slowest speed, one spot, long gaps between balls. Play the stroke you are learning in sets of 10.
Your partner hits easy, slow balls to one spot with no pressure. Play the stroke you are learning, 10 at a time.
Drop the ball and play the stroke you are learning gently against the rebound board, one ball at a time. Reset each time.

success.description: 7 of 10 on the table with the right shape.

coachingPoints: Shape before speed
One cue at a time
Reset to ready between balls

name: Shadow strokes with the 3D player
purpose: Learn the shape of a stroke without a ball by copying the 3D player.

variants.instructions: Open the move in follow-along mode. Copy the player in sets of 10 slow reps, holding your bat. Return to ready after every rep. If you have a mirror, check your shape side-on.

coachingPoints: Slow and exact beats fast and sloppy
Feel the turn of your waist
Always end in ready

name: Shadow combinations
purpose: Link strokes and steps without a ball: push, step, drive, recover.

variants.instructions: Repeat this pattern for 45 seconds, rest 15: backhand push, side step to the forehand, forehand drive, side step back, backhand drive. Then make up your own 3-shot pattern.

success.description: 4 rounds with clean recovery every time.

coachingPoints: Feet move before the arm
Stay low between strokes
Breathe out on each stroke

name: Push, then drive
purpose: Switch from a push to an attacking stroke when the ball sits up.

variants.instructions: Push rally on the backhand. After 3 to 5 pushes your partner pushes long to your forehand: drive it. Start again.
Feeder sends 2 backspin balls to your backhand (push them), then 1 topspin ball to your forehand (drive it).
variants.feederInstructions: 2 backspin to the backhand, then 1 topspin to the forehand. Repeat.

variants.instructions: Robot alternates backspin to the backhand and topspin to the forehand. Push, then drive.

success.description: 7 of 10 patterns with both shots on the table.

coachingPoints: Recover to ready after the push
Move your feet before the drive
Change the bat angle: open for push, closed for drive

name: Forehand drive to targets
purpose: Move from consistency to placement: hit chosen spots, not just the table.

variants.instructions: Put a towel or sheet of paper in your partner's forehand corner. Rally cross-court and count how many of 20 drives hit the target zone.
Target in the far forehand corner. 20 balls; count the hits.
Target in the far forehand corner. 20 balls; count the hits.
Mark a spot on the rebound board with tape. Count how many of 20 drives hit near it.

coachingPoints: Aim with your body turn, not your wrist
Same rhythm as before
Look at the target before the ball comes

name: Forehand loop against backspin
purpose: Lift backspin with a brushing, upward swing and land it deep.

variants.instructions: Backspin balls to your forehand, one at a time. Loop each ball onto the table, aiming deep. Sets of 10.
variants.feederInstructions: Backspin to their forehand, half-long, with a clear chopping action. Wait until they recover.

variants.instructions: Robot on backspin, slow-medium speed, to your forehand. Loop each ball, sets of 10.
Your partner pushes long to your forehand. Loop it, they block it, you play it out. Start each rally with a push from them.

coachingPoints: Drop the bat below the ball, knees bent
Brush up and forward, legs push first
Contact at the top of the bounce or just after

name: Two-point footwork
purpose: Side-to-side steps between forehand and middle, staying low and balanced.

variants.instructions: Your partner blocks one ball to your forehand corner and one to the middle, alternating. Play forehands from both spots.
Balls alternate between your forehand corner and the middle. Forehand from both.
variants.feederInstructions: Alternate forehand corner and middle, steady pace. Speed up when they are comfortable.

variants.instructions: Robot oscillating between two points: forehand corner and middle. Forehand from both.
Two markers 1 metre apart. Side-step between them and play a shadow forehand at each, 30 seconds on, 15 off.

coachingPoints: Small steps, don't cross your feet
Stay at the same height
Arrive before the ball

name: Side-step pattern
purpose: Learn the basic side step without a ball.

variants.instructions: From ready, take two small side steps to your forehand and back. Then add a shadow stroke at each end. 30 seconds on, 15 off.

success.description: 4 rounds staying low the whole time.

coachingPoints: Push off the outside foot
Keep feet wider than shoulders
Head stays level

name: Falkenberg drill
purpose: The classic 3-ball pattern: backhand, pivot forehand, wide forehand.

variants.instructions: Your partner plays to your backhand, backhand again, then to your forehand. You: backhand, pivot and forehand from the backhand corner, then wide forehand. Repeat.
Backhand, backhand (pivot forehand), forehand wide. Repeat.
variants.feederInstructions: Backhand, backhand, forehand. Keep a steady rhythm.

variants.instructions: Robot in a 3-ball pattern if it can: backhand, backhand, forehand. Backhand, pivot forehand, wide forehand.

coachingPoints: Pivot early with a big first step
Recover to the middle after the wide forehand
Stay low throughout

name: Random forehand or backhand
purpose: Decide quickly: the ball can go to either side.

variants.instructions: Your partner blocks to anywhere on your half of the table. You play everything back to their backhand.
Feeder sends balls randomly to your forehand or backhand.
variants.feederInstructions: Random forehand or backhand, no pattern. Medium pace.

variants.instructions: Robot on random placement across the table. Play every ball back.

coachingPoints: Read the direction early
Return to the middle after every ball
Choose fast, then commit

name: Backspin serve practice
purpose: A legal serve with clear backspin and low height.

variants.instructions: Serve backspin to your partner. They push it back gently so you can see the spin. Aim for the ball to bounce twice on their side if they let it.
Take a basket of balls and serve backspin. Watch if the ball stops or comes back after it bounces on the far side.
variants.feederInstructions: No feeding needed; collect balls at the far end.

variants.instructions: Robot off. Take a basket of balls and serve backspin. Watch if the ball stops or comes back.
Table half down. Serve backspin and check the ball's second bounce on the far side.
No table: practise the legal toss. Ball on your flat, open palm, toss straight up at least 16 cm, and brush under it as it falls. 20 tosses.

success.description: 6 of 10 serves bounce twice on the far side.

coachingPoints: Toss straight up, at least 16 cm, ball visible
Open bat, brush under the back of the ball
Contact low, close to the table height

name: Short and long serve targets
purpose: Control length: the same motion, two very different serves.

variants.instructions: Two targets: a towel near the net (short) and one near the end line (long). Alternate short and long. Your partner tells you which landed.
Basket of balls, two targets: short near the net and long near the end line. Alternate.
variants.feederInstructions: Collect balls and tell them where each serve bounced.

variants.instructions: Robot off. Basket of balls, two targets. Alternate short and long.
Table half down. Two targets. Alternate short and long.

success.description: 6 of 10 serves land in the right zone.

coachingPoints: Same toss and motion for both
Short: first bounce near the net on your side
Long: first bounce near your end line

name: Receive with a push
purpose: Read a backspin serve and push it back low and safe.

variants.instructions: Your partner serves backspin anywhere. You push every serve back low and deep. Then swap roles.
The feeder serves backspin from their end. Push each one back.
variants.feederInstructions: Serve backspin from your end with a basket. Vary the placement.

variants.instructions: Robot on backspin with random placement. Push each ball back low.

coachingPoints: Watch the server's bat at contact
Move in with your foot for short balls
Push deep to their backhand by default

name: Push and drive game
purpose: A small game: push until someone can attack, then play it out.

variants.instructions: Games to 11. Serve backspin. Push until one of you gets a long or high ball, then attack it. A point won with your first attack counts 2.

success.description: Win 3 points with your first attack.

coachingPoints: Be patient, wait for the right ball
Recover after every push
Use your pre-point routine

name: Rally record challenge
purpose: A solo game: beat your best rally count under a little pressure.

variants.instructions: Robot on random forehand/backhand. Three tries to beat your record. Between tries, do your pre-point routine.
Rebound board up. Alternate forehand and backhand. Three tries to beat your record.
Feeder plays random topspin. Three tries to beat your record.
variants.feederInstructions: Random forehand or backhand, a bit faster than in practice.

variants.instructions: Cooperative: you both try to set a new rally record with forehand and backhand anywhere on the table.

coachingPoints: Treat every try like a match point
Breathe out before you start
Stay relaxed as the count grows

name: Serve and attack the third ball
purpose: Short backspin serve, long push comes back, forehand attack.

variants.instructions: Serve short backspin. Your partner pushes long anywhere on your half. Loop the third ball, then play the point out.
Serve short; the feeder immediately sends a long backspin ball to your forehand or backhand. Attack it.
variants.feederInstructions: After their serve, feed one long backspin ball to a random side.

variants.instructions: Serve a shadow serve, then the robot sends long backspin. Loop it.

success.description: 6 of 10 third balls on the table.

coachingPoints: After the serve, step back into ready at once
Expect the long push and be ready to move
Loop with spin first, speed second

name: Lateral hops
purpose: Quick, springy legs for fast side-to-side movement.

variants.instructions: Hop side to side over a line on two feet for 20 seconds, rest 20. Then single-leg hops, 10 each leg. 3 rounds.

coachingPoints: Land softly on the balls of your feet
Knees over toes
Stop if anything hurts

name: Quick steps
purpose: Fast feet without jumping.

variants.instructions: Fast small steps on the spot for 15 seconds, then a side step left and right for 15 seconds, then rest 15. 4 rounds.

coachingPoints: Stay on the balls of your feet
Arms relaxed
Keep your chest up

name: Core and shoulder care
purpose: A strong middle and healthy shoulders for a long playing life.

variants.instructions: 2 rounds: 30-second plank, 30-second side plank each side, 15 slow shoulder external rotations each arm (light band or water bottle), 10 wrist curls each way.

coachingPoints: Straight line from head to heels
Slow and controlled
Light weight is enough

name: Pre-point routine
purpose: The same short routine before every point, so you start each one calm and clear.

variants.instructions: Build your routine: turn away from the table, one slow breath out, wipe the bat or touch the table, decide your serve and your plan for the next ball, then step in. Rehearse it 10 times.

coachingPoints: Same steps every time
Decide one simple plan
Let the last point go

name: Breathing reset
purpose: A tool to calm down after a mistake or before a big point.

variants.instructions: Breathe in through your nose for 4 counts, hold for 2, breathe out slowly for 6. Do 6 rounds. Then do 2 rounds while picturing a tight game.

coachingPoints: The out-breath is longer than the in-breath
Shoulders drop on every out-breath
Use it between points

name: Cool-down
purpose: Bring your heart rate down and stretch the muscles you used.

variants.instructions: Slow walk for one minute. Then hold each stretch for 20 to 30 seconds: calves, thighs (front and back), hips, chest in a doorway, and the forearm of your playing arm.

coachingPoints: Hold, don't bounce
Breathe slowly
Note one thing that went well today
